title: Deterministic Quantization Manifests and Signed Artifact Versioning
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8 profiles, calibration caches, validator traces) are generated by non-deterministic calibration runs and currently stored in the artifact store without strong, verifiable versioning. That makes reproducing past calibrations, diagnosing accuracy regressions, and performing safe rollbacks difficult for Dedicated and Private customers.

Goal: Provide a deterministic calibration pipeline plus a signed manifest and immutable artifact versioning scheme that captures: calibration RNG seeds, toolchain versions, model git commit, quant profile parameters, calibration input metadata, and a cryptographic provenance chain (hash + optional KMS signature). This enables reproducible artifact regeneration, traceable audits, and safe staged rollback with automated validation checks.
acceptance_criteria: Each quant artifact produced by the calibration pipeline must be accompanied by a manifest file containing: model_commit, calibration_seed, pipeline_version, toolchain_hash, training_tokenizer_hash, input_sample_signature, output_summary_metrics, and list_of_files with sha256 checksums.
Manifest files are SHA256-signed by the team's KMS key and stored immutably in the artifact store with a content-addressable path (artifacts/{sha256(manifest)}).

A restore operation (given a manifest id) can reproduce the exact artifact by re-running the calibration pipeline and producing identical checksums within tolerances for floating-point operations (documented).

CI gates that accept a new quant profile into production must run a deterministic re-calibration and an accuracy validation job against a stored QA set; any regression > 0.25% absolute on critical metrics blocks rollout.
Rollbacks can reference older manifest IDs; the console can perform a staged canary rollback running the validation job automatically before switching routes.
proposed_solution: 1) Deterministic calibration runner: add explicit RNG seeding for every stochastic step (sample ordering, shuffling, dropout simulation), capture environment variables and CPU/GPU kernels used. Use fixed precision math flags where available. 2) Manifest schema: single-file JSON manifest that lists every produced file with SHA256, named inputs (dataset slice id, sample list checksum), exact pipeline binary digest (docker image sha/OCI digest), and a human-readable changelog. 3) Content-addressable storage layout: store artifacts under artifacts/{manifest_sha256}/..., manifest filename = manifest.json. 4) Signing: use KMS-backed signing to seal manifests; store public key metadata in config for verification. 5) CI integration: calibration jobs run in hermetic CI image; result manifests are verified and pushed to artifact store only if signatures/checksums pass. 6) Backwards compatibility: support an import adapter to accept legacy artifacts by computing best-effort manifest and marking provenance as partial. 7) Rollback workflow: console exposes manifest history per-model; rollback triggers a re-validation job that runs the same deterministic pipeline and compares metrics within tolerance. 8) Audit & retention: metadata indexed in searchable index (artifact registry) with retention policy and exportable audit trail.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (baseline): implement manifest schema + deterministic runner in a feature branch; unit tests for RNG seeding and checksum computation.
Phase 2 (CI integration): add calibration job in CI with hermetic image; require signed manifest; block merges without passing artifact verification.
Phase 3 (artifact registry): implement content-addressable storage and index; expose simple REST endpoints for lookup and verification.
Phase 4 (console + rollback): console UI to list manifests and perform staged rollback with automatic validation jobs and canary routing.
Phase 5 (migration): run import adapter to convert latest legacy artifacts and run re-calibration to generate signed manifests for high-priority models.
migration_steps: Inventory existing quant artifacts and prioritize by usage and customer impact.
For top-20 artifacts, run the deterministic runner with recorded inputs to generate candidate manifests and compare checksums; hand-audit any mismatches.
For artifacts that cannot be reproduced exactly, attach a partial-provenance manifest documenting missing fields and mark as 'legacy'.
Backfill registry entries and add UI flags to indicate 'reproducible' vs 'legacy'.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for manifest builder and sha256 computation (edge cases: large file streaming).
Determinism smoke tests that run the calibration 10x in CI and assert file checksums match exactly for kernel-consistent inputs (or within documented FP tolerance).
Accuracy regression suite: run validation set and assert no regression > 0.25% absolute on prioritized metrics.
End-to-end test: simulate a rollback via manifest reference and verify the console correctly triggers validation and route swap on success.
notes: Decision: use SHA256 for checksums and manifest identity; signature performed with KMS ECDSA key to allow verification in Dedicated/Private customers (public key exportable).

Trade-off: strict determinism may require locking certain kernel variants; we will document supported hardware/kernel combinations and fall back to 'best-effort' manifests if exact reproduction is impossible on different hardware.
Follow-up: investigate lightweight binary diffs for large kv_cache.bin files to reduce storage for iterative calibration runs.
Security: manifest contains minimal PII and dataset checksums only; sign manifest instead of encrypting to keep artifacts sharable across teams.
